title: Words Beside the Camera
paras: In the early days of television, speakers often held paper notes or learned their lines by heart. There was a clear [[similarity|similarity]] between their work and acting on a stage: both depended on memory. However, a newsreader describing a new [[weapon|weapon]] could not change important details simply because a word was forgotten.

In the early 1950s, a machine called a teleprompter offered help. A long roll of paper moved inside a [[frame|frame]] near the camera. Large letters made the text easy to read, while an [[arrow|arrow]] showed the speaker which line to follow. The paper needed to be a suitable [[grade|grade]] so that it would move smoothly without tearing.

The machine could not stop a dry [[throat|throat]], but it removed some of the fear of forgetting. A nervous speaker might finally [[dare|dare]] to look towards the camera and feel more [[confident|confident]]. It also helped actors preparing an [[episode|episode]] of a television series, although someone had to move the words at the right speed.

Later designs used glass to place the words directly in front of the camera lens. Viewers saw a face, not a page. [[personally|Personally]], I find this the cleverest part of the invention: a machine helped a prepared speech feel like a conversation.
zh: 在电视发展的早期，讲话者常常手拿纸质笔记，或者背熟台词。他们的工作与舞台表演有一个明显的相似点：两者都依赖记忆。然而，新闻播报员在介绍一种新武器时，不能仅仅因为忘了某个词就改变重要细节。
20世纪50年代初，一种叫作提词器的机器提供了帮助。一长卷纸在摄像机附近的框架内移动。大号字让文字容易辨认，而箭头则指示讲话者该读哪一行。纸张需要达到合适的质量等级，才能顺畅移动而不被撕破。
这台机器无法防止喉咙发干，却能减轻人们对忘词的恐惧。紧张的讲话者或许终于敢于朝摄像机看去，并且感到更有自信。它也帮助了正在准备某一集电视剧的演员，不过仍然需要有人以合适的速度移动文字。
后来的设计利用玻璃，将文字呈现在摄像机镜头正前方。观众看到的是一张面孔，而不是一页纸。就我个人而言，我觉得这是这项发明最巧妙的地方：一台机器让事先准备好的讲话听起来像是在聊天。

q.s: Early television speakers and stage actors both needed to remember what they would say.
q.why: 首段指出两者都依赖记忆。

q.s: The first teleprompters displayed their text on glass rather than paper.
q.why: 早期提词器使用纸卷，后来才用玻璃。

q.s: Actors learned to use teleprompters more quickly than newsreaders did.
q.why: 文中未比较演员与播报员的学习速度。
